en-US.description: A powerful clipboard manager for Windows
en-US.longDescription:
ClipMate is a modern clipboard manager that helps you manage your clipboard history,
organize clips into collections, and boost your productivity with powerful features
like PowerPaste, Quick Paste, and advanced text manipulation tools.
en-US.name: ClipMate
en-US.releaseNotes:
ClipMate 1.2.0-beta.1
Downloads
───────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Package                                │Size      │Description
───────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ClipMate-Setup-1.2.0-beta.1.exe        │~106.32 MB│Recommended - auto-installs dependencies
───────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ClipMate-Portable-1.2.0-beta.1.zip     │~155.46 MB│Portable - requires .NET 10 & WebView2 pre-installed
───────────────────────────────────────┴──────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Installation
WinGet:
winget install Tsabo.ClipMate
Installer (Recommended):
- Target OS: Windows 11 or Windows 10 version 1809+
- Auto-installs if needed: .NET 10 Desktop Runtime, ASP.NET Core 10 Runtime, WebView2 Runtime
- Simply download and run - dependencies handled automatically
Portable:
- Extract ZIP and run ClipMate.exe
- Requires .NET 10 Desktop Runtime and ASP.NET Core 10 Runtime pre-installed
- Requires WebView2 Runtime (usually pre-installed on Windows 11)
Security
✅ Code Signed - The installer, uninstaller and ClipMate binaries are signed by Jeremy Brown (Certum)
Verification
SHA-256 Checksums:
# Verify installer
(Get-FileHash ClipMate-Setup-1.2.0-beta.1.exe).Hash -eq (Get-Content ClipMate-Setup-1.2.0-beta.1.exe.sha256).Split()[0]
# Verify portable
(Get-FileHash ClipMate-Portable-1.2.0-beta.1.zip).Hash -eq (Get-Content ClipMate-Portable-1.2.0-beta.1.zip.sha256).Split()[0]
What's Changed
Added
- Hide Clips From Other Programs - A new option on the Pasting options page, off by default. While PowerPaste is on, programs in the background get nothing from the clipboard, so they can't make it repeat a clip or make a paste put in nothing. Clipboard history, other clipboard managers, and Remote Desktop and WSL clipboard sharing don't see the clips until PowerPaste stops.
Changed
- PowerPaste Button - The button now works as in ClipMate 7. A click starts in the direction you last used (going up the first time), and the next click turns it off. Turning it off without pasting makes the next start go the other way. PowerPaste Up and PowerPaste Down turn it off if it's already going that way.
- Clicking Another Clip During PowerPaste - As in ClipMate 7, clicking a clip outside the series takes PowerPaste back to the start of the series. It used to turn PowerPaste off.
- PowerPaste Shield - The option is back on the Pasting options page, and it now works. It's on by default, so other programs reading the clipboard don't move PowerPaste on. If PowerPaste doesn't advance when you paste into a program, turn it off: then any program reading the clipboard moves PowerPaste on, as in ClipMate 7 with its shield off.
Fixed
- Case Conversion - Edit > Case Conversion opened an empty submenu, and the same commands on the tray menu only reported a future update. It now offers lower case (Ctrl+Alt+L), UPPER CASE (Ctrl+Alt+U), Mixed Case (Ctrl+Alt+M), Sentence case. (Ctrl+Alt+S) and iNVERT cASE (Ctrl+Alt+I). As in ClipMate 7, each converts the text and title of every selected clip and leaves the clip with only its text. Encrypted clips and clips without text are skipped.
- Clean-Up Text, Remove Linebreaks and Strip Out Non-TEXT Data Formats - These Edit menu commands did nothing but report a future update. They now work on every selected clip, as in ClipMate 7, and leave each clip with only its text. Clean-Up Text... opens a new Text Cleanup Options window, also used by the editor toolbar, which remembers your choices. Hold Ctrl while choosing Remove Linebreaks to remove the line breaks between paragraphs too, or Shift to join lines without a space. Remove Line Breaks on the editor toolbar now joins lines the same way, and no longer leaves stray characters behind in text with Windows line breaks.
- PowerPaste With One Clip Selected - PowerPaste pasted the clip once and stopped. As in ClipMate 7, it now runs from that clip to the end of the collection, and the clip list follows along. With several clips selected, it still pastes only those.
- PowerPaste in Browsers, Windows Terminal and Store Apps - Pasting into these programs didn't count as a paste, so PowerPaste never advanced. Now it does.
- PowerPaste Missing Pastes - A paste soon after the previous one could go unnoticed, and the next paste repeated the clip. This happened most on machines running WSL or in a remote session.
- Pasting Quickly With PowerPaste - Pastes less than half a second apart repeated the same clip. Pastes about a quarter of a second apart or more now advance.
- Pastes Lost While PowerPaste Is On - With WSL or Remote Desktop running, their clipboard client could keep reading the clipboard for as long as PowerPaste was on, mostly on a busy computer. That kept the clipboard busy, so a paste could put in nothing, or not move on to the next clip. A program in the background that keeps reading is now refused the clip until PowerPaste next starts, and the clipboard stays quiet.
- Clicking a Clip Right After a Paste - A click just before PowerPaste moved on to the next clip was ignored, and the next paste used the wrong clip. On a busy computer, the clicked row could also stay highlighted after PowerPaste went back to the start of its sequence.
- PowerPaste Stuck on a Clip - When another program kept the clipboard open just as PowerPaste moved on, the next clip never came up, and every paste repeated the last one. PowerPaste now keeps trying until the clip is on the clipboard.
- Exploding PowerPaste Going Up - Each clip's fragments now paste in reading order when going up. They used to paste last to first.
- Reset Buttons Do What They Say - The Layout/Font, Application Profile and Everything buttons on the Advanced options tab reported success without changing anything. Now Layout/Font resets ClipMate Classic's position and size and the editor font the next time ClipMate starts. Application Profile clears the Application Profile at once, with no restart. Everything clears the Application Profile, turns off Start with Windows and resets all other settings the next time ClipMate starts. It keeps your Databases, saved searches and paired Devices. The mention of re-registering is gone from its tooltip, since ClipMate has no licensing.
- Source URL on the HTML Tab - The Source box said "(No source URL found)" for clips that had a source URL, even while the clip list's Source URL column showed it. It now shows the clip's source URL, and Go opens it.
- Help Links - Help in the encryption key dialog opened a page that doesn't exist, and so did the localization link in About. They now open the Options documentation and GitHub Issues.
Full Changelog: CHANGELOG.md
